title: Reactive Variables
description: Learn to use Apollo Client reactive variables for managing local state outside the GraphQL cache.

data.text: Reactive variables are Apollo Client's mechanism for storing non-GraphQL local state. Unlike query variables, reactive variables are not tied to a specific query or component. Any component that reads the variable will re-render when it changes.

data.title: Creating and using reactive variables

items: UI state that does not belong in the GraphQL schema: theme, modals, form inputs.
Global flags: authentication status, feature flags.
Transient state: current step in a wizard, selected filters.
data.title: Use Cases

data.text: Reactive variables are the simplest way to share state across components without Context providers. Use them for simple global state and reserve Context for more complex dependency injection.
data.title: State Simplicity
Reactive Variables Key Points
points: Reactive variables store non-GraphQL local state.
They trigger re-renders in subscribed components.
Use makeVar() to create a reactive variable.
Ideal for simple global UI state.
data.takeaway: Reactive variables provide a lightweight, Apollo-native solution for local state management.
